nodes.label: docs/canon/raw/user_turns_all.md — the corpus: the user's own human-authored turns, chronological, verbatim text with no edits, and the only first-hand evidence of what he asked for. The file's own header line reads "920 turns"; the body carries 929 turn headers spanning 2026-05-14 12:30 → 2026-08-06 10:46, desktop 127 + laptop 802, across 5,223 lines. Cited as turns:L<line>, the line in this .md rendering; the machine-readable twin is the .jsonl beside it. Produced by python tools/canon_extract.py and read-only — re-derive rather than edit. Any claim about the user's intent cites a turn here by line; no turn, no claim.

Corpus format and how to cite it. Each turn is a `## <YYYY-MM-DD> <HH:MM> · <machine> · <session-uuid>.jsonl` heading followed by the verbatim turn text; pasted material is marked `*paste / file drop · N chars*`. Citations across docs/canon/ take the form turns:L<line> = the line in this .md rendering. The machine-readable twin is user_turns_all.jsonl, one JSON object per turn carrying uuid, iso_timestamp, machine and text, and it is what the CQ search in REVIEW_WORKLIST.md reads. The file is evidence and read-only — re-derive with tools/canon_extract.py, never edit

Corpus band 2026-07-06, L474-L659, 44 turns — the day the v1 concept is restated in full and the arm is renamed. Holds the fullest single statement of the v1 concept in the corpus (file → chunks → tags, chunk description and relational weight to file, tags with relational values, facet-values on tags, all of it embedded, no content in the graph); "but the actual content should never exist in the graph at all, and we fixed that by just making pointers again, right?"
